_trusted_proxies_note: The peers whose X-Forwarded-For this oracle believes. Behind a reverse proxy every request arrives from loopback, and keying a rate limit on that gives the whole internet one bucket -- one flooder then locks every auditor out of the log that exists to be audited.
_precisions_note: Every asset named in `markets` needs an entry. A missing one is assumed to have 8 decimals, and where that is wrong the price is signed wrong by a power of ten -- which no signature check downstream can catch. A config that names some and not others is refused at start.
_log_note: Rotate the attestation log past this many bytes (0 never rotates). The closed file's digest is published beside it and seeded into the next file's running hash, so /v1/digest still commits to every attestation ever signed. Rotate ONLY this way: an outside rename or truncate desynchronises the running hash from the file.
_source_note: `max_age` is how long a fetched snapshot may be reused. `feed_max_age` is how old the feed's own `_meta.updated` may be before this oracle refuses to re-sign its numbers -- OFF unless you set it, because a feed is not obliged to publish that field and most do not, the node repository's mock price server included. Set it only against a feed that does: an oracle asked for a check it cannot perform refuses to sign rather than treat 'cannot tell' as 'fresh'. `type` may also be `http` (one request per market, which honours `max_age` as a per-symbol cache) or `static` (fixed prices, for drills). A key a source does not understand is refused at start rather than ignored: a setting that goes nowhere is one you believe is protecting you.
_previous_keys_note: x-only keys this oracle used to sign with, published at /v1/pubkey so a borrower's page can tell a rotation from a stranger. A live vault bakes the key it was originated against, so rotation is never a swap.
